THEATRE REVIEW WHALE RIDING WEATHER

Friday, November 13, 1992

ROBERT CUSHMAN

Toronto ONT -- WRITTEN BY BRYDEN MacDONALD Directed by Annie Kidder At the Factory Theatre Rating: Bryden MacDonald's Whale Riding Weather is dedicated to the propositions that all we have is one another and that love will conquer all Whale Riding delivers maximum voltage BY ROBERT CUSHMAN Special to The Globe and Mail Toronto ALLAN Gray is the first actor I have seen who can act with the whites of his eyes. Or maybe, since I'm terribly unobservant, he is just the first actor I have noticed doing it. In Whale Riding Weather, performed now by the same cast that originated it last year, there is a moment in which Gray looks at a lover - by this time an ex-lover - with pupils that are absolutely dead. That may be expected. What surprises and alarms is that the sockets encasing them look so blank, weary, hopeless: whiter than white.
